key_insight: Sparse sensor data plus phase-amplitude reduction and machine learning can compute optimal actuation that rapidly synchronizes airfoil wake shedding while controlling lift fluctuations.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical route to faster post-stall flow control and safer aerodynamic actuation when output fluctuations must be constrained.
method: Use three sparse sensors and nonlinear ML reconstruction to estimate the wake state.
Derive time-varying phase and amplitude sensitivity fields to locate when and where forcing is most effective.
Analytically design an optimal waveform that accelerates frequency locking with an amplitude penalty on lift variation.
evidence_signal: The approach was tested on several NACA airfoils at multiple post-stall angles of attack, where the optimized forcing changed wake frequency faster than sinusoidal actuation and reduced lift fluctuations by 20% with amplitude penalty.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurate sparse-sensor reconstruction and periodic vortex-shedding behavior, so robustness may drop if the flow becomes strongly nonperiodic or sensor coverage is insufficient.
paper_title: Machine-learning-assisted phase-amplitude reduction for fast synchronization of airfoil wakes with constrained fluctuations
